data.narrative:
Cognition is a Series A-stage AI & Software company founded by Scott Wu, Steven Hao, and Walden Yan that has raised over $400M to date. Valuation analysis draws on a comparison set of five same-sector, same/adjacent-stage private peers (Scale AI, Reflection AI, Physical Intelligence, Black Forest Labs, and Field AI), supplemented by one public comparable (Palantir, ticker PLTR), alongside a broader universe of eight private frontier-tech companies.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using the $400M+ total raised as a proxy baseline, applied a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement, yielding an implied value of $9M. The peer-median method drew on the five-company comparables, which show a median valuation of $5.6B with a range spanning $2.0B to $29.0B. This approach yields an implied value of $5.6B, reflecting Cognition's positioning within a cohort of well-capitalized frontier-AI businesses.

The triangulated analysis across both methods supports a valuation range of $8M to $6.4B, with a median implied value of $2.8B. The wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty: peer valuations range across two orders of magnitude, and the stage-progression method's reliance on capital raised as a proxy introduces methodological limitation. Key uncertainties include revenue run-rate and growth trajectory relative to the peer set, particularly given the recency of frontier-model commercialization.
